rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - r7-d1-locale-migration [ses_f16938623ffeZpsFDzWm2DHToT].md:L3724] **make the migration correct under the worst case.** If cascade doesn't fire, the restore is a no-op-ish (delete + reinsert same rows). If it fires, the restore brings the rows back. Either way correct.

nodes.label: An autocommit probe makes PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys look broken, because the pragma is reset at the end of every statement when no transaction spans them
nodes.norm_label: an autocommit probe makes pragma defer foreign keys look broken because the pragma is reset at the end of every statement when no transaction spans them

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - r7-d1-locale-migration [ses_f16938623ffeZpsFDzWm2DHToT].md:L6997] D1 executes a `--file` upload as one unit, so the pragma does span the file.

nodes.label: The RENAME is issued from the scratch table name, never from the live table, because with legacy_alter_table=off RENAME rewrites REFERENCES clauses naming the renamed table

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - r7-d1-locale-migration [ses_f16938623ffeZpsFDzWm2DHToT].md:L4355] The child FK clause is **not** rewritten by the rename (it still says `REFERENCES blog_tags(id)`), so `legacy_alter_table=OFF` is safe here — because the rename source is `blog_tags_new`, which nothing references.
